programs.name: Double the Donation Matching and Workplace Giving
programs.summary: Software for nonprofits and schools that identifies employer matching, volunteer-grant, payroll-giving, and corporate-sponsorship opportunities and guides supporters through employer-specific next steps.

content.summary: Double the Donation provides matching-gift and workplace-giving automation for nonprofits and schools.

best_for: Nonprofits and educational institutions with donation or volunteer activity that want to identify and automate workplace-giving opportunities.
considerations: Double the Donation does not disburse employer funds; payment timing and approval remain with each employer or foundation.
Published plan eligibility and pricing vary by organization size, contribution volume, and required integrations.

best_for: Nonprofits and grant teams seeking a centralized workflow from prospect research through award and spend tracking.

Plan prices, users, and pre-award or post-award capabilities differ materially.

programs.name: Charity Digital and Livestream Fundraising
programs.summary: Individuals create digital, livestream, fitness, or team campaigns for an approved charitable cause using rewards, polls, milestones, match challenges, employer matching, and streaming integrations.

value.description: Third-party processor fee depends on the charity's activated PayPal, PayPal Giving Fund, Stripe, or Giving Block account and negotiated terms
Tiltify contribution fee varies by charity plan; Tiltify states its current processing average is less than 5%

caveats: A charity may enable an option for donors to cover this fee

participation_requirements: A cause must be a charitable organization, and registration must be submitted by an authorized representative.
Fundraisers create and verify a Tiltify account before launching a campaign.
other_restrictions: The cause may be asked for additional verification information before approval.
requirements.editorial_summary: Charitable causes are reviewed by Tiltify before supporters can fundraise for them.

notes: Cause approval usually takes 5–7 business days. Donations go directly to the charity's activated payment processor in real time.

Fundraisers build and share campaign pages, can add incentives and schedules, form teams, stream on supported services, or connect digital fitness, while the charity receives donations through its own processor.

programs.name: Tiltify Personal Fundraising
programs.summary: A personal crowdfunding program for raising money for oneself or another person through campaign pages, optional supporting fundraisers, rewards, polls, livestreams, fitness challenges, video, audio, merchandise, or in-person events.

other_restrictions: The fundraiser country is selected during creation and cannot be changed; unsupported or ineligible campaigns may be refunded and removed.
requirements.editorial_summary: Personal campaigns may support educational, medical, emergency, animal, sports, memorial, veterans, faith, family, travel, event, or community needs.

notes: Funds are held for 14 days before being sent to the connected account on a rolling basis; subsequent processor settlement time was not established.
The recipient creates a page and can allow linked supporting campaigns; identity verification and a connected bank account are required before publication and withdrawal.

geography.notes: Tiltify describes cause fundraising as global. Tiltify Personal currently publishes 20 supported payout countries; cause and processor availability can differ.

content.summary: Tiltify supports digital, livestream, gaming, fitness, charity, and personal fundraising campaigns.
content.how_it_works: A fundraiser selects an approved charity or creates a verified personal campaign, builds a shareable page, adds interactive tools such as milestones or polls, and can raise through streaming, fitness, teams, video, social, or in-person outreach.
best_for: Charities, creators, gaming communities, teams, and individuals seeking interactive digital fundraising and livestream integrations.
considerations: Charity and personal programs have different eligibility, money flow, geography, and timing.
Charity fees vary by plan and processor; personal transfers requiring currency conversion add 1–2%.

programs.name: Order Form Coffee Fundraiser
programs.summary: Group members collect local orders for coffee and tea, submit the sold quantities, receive a consolidated shipment, and distribute products to supporters.

notes: Shipping is free for 100 or more items delivered to a commercial address; smaller orders can incur shipping.

participation_requirements: The group collects orders before submitting its product order and coordinates distribution after delivery.
requirements.editorial_summary: There is no registration fee, upfront product purchase, or minimum commitment for order-form sales.

notes: Giving Bean roasts, packs, and ships the consolidated sold order to the group, which delivers items to supporters; custom coffee labels are available at no extra charge.

programs.name: Online Coffee Fundraising Store
programs.summary: A group shares its online fundraising link while Giving Bean processes purchases, ships coffee and tea directly to supporters, and credits 25% on most items to the group.

caveats: The published 25% applies to most items

participation_requirements: The group registers and shares its supplied link or group name through email, social media, or other outreach.
requirements.editorial_summary: The online store has no registration fee, upfront inventory, or minimum commitment.

notes: The online fundraiser may remain active year-round; the source does not specify whether the 2–10 fulfillment days are calendar or business days.
Giving Bean handles online ordering and direct shipment to supporter homes or offices; subscriptions can continue generating group earnings through repeat orders.

geography.notes: Giving Bean states that it supports groups throughout the United States.

content.summary: Giving Bean offers coffee and tea fundraising through local order forms or a direct-ship online store.
content.how_it_works: A group chooses local preorder sales for 40% profit and group distribution, or an online link for 25% on most sales with provider fulfillment and no inventory.
best_for: Schools, churches, teams, missions, and community groups seeking coffee and tea products with local or direct-ship fulfillment.
considerations: Profit and fulfillment differ by program: 40% with group distribution versus 25% on most direct-ship store items.
Free consolidated shipping requires at least 100 items and delivery to a commercial address.

caveats: Shipping charges on qualifying smaller brochure orders can reduce effective profit

notes: There is no minimum order. Collective brochure orders of 35 or more items receive free shipping.

programs.name: Brochure Flower Bulb Fundraiser
programs.summary: Group members take brochure orders for seasonal bulbs and plants, submit one collective order, retain 50% profit, and distribute the delivered products to supporters.

participation_requirements: The group collects supporter orders and payment, submits the collective order through its dashboard, pays Dutch Mill Bulbs' share, and distributes the shipment promptly.
other_restrictions: Products are seasonal living plant material and all submitted orders are final.
requirements.editorial_summary: There is no minimum order; free brochure-order shipping requires at least 35 items.

notes: Most groups run for 2–3 weeks within the published spring or fall selling windows. The group keeps its brochure profit when submitting the order rather than waiting for a separate payout.
Dutch Mill Bulbs ships the collective seasonal order to the organization; the organization is responsible for timely supporter distribution and handling distribution questions.

programs.name: Online Flower Bulb Fundraiser
programs.summary: Supporters buy bulbs and plants through the group's unique link or QR code, Dutch Mill Bulbs ships directly to their entered addresses, and the group earns 50% of online sales.

participation_requirements: The group registers, sets dates within a spring or fall selling season, and shares its unique URL or QR code.
other_restrictions: Online shipping excludes Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, and APO/FPO addresses.
requirements.editorial_summary: There is no minimum order or inventory requirement.

notes: Profit disbursements are processed in bi-weekly batches and paid within 30 days of fundraiser close when the account is in good standing. The frozen cadence enum does not encode bi-weekly schedules.
Supporters pay online and receive direct seasonal shipment with tracking. Online profit offsets any brochure balance first; excess profit is disbursed after close.

geography.notes: Programs serve the contiguous 48 United States; direct shipment excludes Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, and APO/FPO addresses.

content.summary: Dutch Mill Bulbs offers seasonal flower-bulb and plant fundraisers through brochures, online direct shipping, or a combination.
content.how_it_works: A group registers for a spring or fall selling window, shares brochures or a unique online link, and earns 50% while group-distributed and direct-ship orders follow different payment and logistics flows.
best_for: Schools, teams, PTOs, scouts, clubs, and community groups seeking a seasonal flowers-and-plants fundraiser.
considerations: Products and shipping dates are seasonal and orders are final.
Online profit is credited against any brochure balance before an excess payout is issued.

programs.name: SaveAround Coupon Book Fundraiser
programs.summary: Groups sell market-specific physical coupon books in person or through a custom online store, with SaveAround fulfilling online orders and the group handling in-person book distribution and closeout.

participation_requirements: The group applies or works with a representative, distributes physical books for in-person sales, tracks payments, and completes the campaign closeout.
other_restrictions: Book editions and included savings are market-specific.
requirements.editorial_summary: SaveAround markets coupon-book fundraising to schools, teams, religious groups, arts groups, and community organizations with no upfront cost.

notes: Groups can collect in-person card payments and fulfill those books themselves; a custom SupportOurGroups store can reach supporters nationwide, with SaveAround shipping online orders directly.

programs.name: SaveAround Digital Pass Fundraiser
programs.summary: A group shares a custom link to sell a year-long mobile and printable savings pass with local and national offers, while SaveAround tracks sales and pays the group's agreed share.

conditions: Exact rate is confirmed during onboarding and depends on campaign size and length

participation_requirements: The group applies and confirms its campaign scope, terms, and profit share with a SaveAround representative.
requirements.editorial_summary: There is no upfront purchase, minimum order, inventory, printing, or shipping requirement.

notes: A representative responds within one business day, but the page does not guarantee full setup in that time. The pass is available instantly; most groups receive check or ACH payout within 30 days of campaign close.
SaveAround supplies a tracked campaign page and link. Supporters receive a mobile pass with printable backup and redeem local or national offers for one year.

geography.notes: SaveAround serves organizations nationwide. Coupon books and many Digital Pass offers are local-market specific, while both programs also expose national offers or supporter reach.

content.summary: SaveAround offers physical coupon-book and digital savings-pass fundraisers for schools and community groups.
content.how_it_works: A group chooses physical books or a no-inventory digital pass, promotes local and national savings, and retains an agreed share while ordering, fulfillment, and payout differ by program.
best_for: Schools, PTAs, sports teams, clubs, churches, arts groups, and nonprofits whose supporters value local and national discounts.
considerations: Physical book availability and offers vary by market.
The Digital Pass profit share is confirmed during onboarding and varies from 50% to 70%.

caveats: Local assortment, product cost, and pricing vary by participating shop and fundraiser format

programs.name: Classic Pre-Sell Fundraiser
programs.summary: A group collects supporter orders before requesting only the doughnuts and other participating-shop fundraising products it needs, then picks up or arranges delivery and distributes them.

participation_requirements: The organizer selects a participating local shop, downloads its current forms and assortment, collects orders, and submits an order request.
other_restrictions: Fundraising pricing is for approved organization or cause fundraising and not for personal gain or commercial resale.
requirements.editorial_summary: Product selection, prices, pickup, and delivery availability depend on the participating local shop.

notes: Fundraising orders require at least three days' lead time; delivery requests require five days.
The group coordinates local pickup or approved delivery and then distributes pre-sold products to supporters.

programs.name: Classic One-Day Sale Fundraiser
programs.summary: A group orders fresh doughnuts in advance, picks them up from a participating shop, and sells them during a one-day event or community sale.

participation_requirements: The organizer chooses a participating shop, requests the fundraising order in advance, buys the products, and manages the sale.
other_restrictions: Fundraising pricing is not intended for personal gain or commercial profit.
requirements.editorial_summary: The group takes inventory risk because products are bought before the one-day sale.

notes: The group purchases and collects fresh product from its local shop and is responsible for on-site selling and any unsold inventory.

programs.name: Digital Dozens Fundraiser
programs.summary: A group shares a custom fundraising link, supporters purchase Digital Dozens coupons delivered by email, and supporters later redeem them in person for Original Glazed dozens at participating shops.

participation_requirements: The organizer creates and shares the Digital Dozens link; supporters use emailed coupons according to the redemption terms.
other_restrictions: Coupons are redeemable only at participating U.S. Krispy Kreme shops, in shop or drive-thru, and not for online orders or delivery.
Coupons exclude Times Square, Puerto Rico, grocery and convenience stores, and locations outside dedicated Krispy Kreme shops.
requirements.editorial_summary: The reviewed current page does not publish a universal minimum or fixed per-coupon profit.

notes: Krispy Kreme emails digital coupons to buyers; supporters handle later in-shop redemption, so the group has no product delivery or inventory.

geography.notes: Programs depend on participating U.S. shops. Digital Dozens explicitly excludes Puerto Rico, Times Square, grocery and convenience stores, and non-dedicated locations.

content.summary: Krispy Kreme Fundraising offers pre-sold, one-day inventory, and digital-coupon doughnut fundraisers.
content.how_it_works: A group selects a participating shop and either pre-sells local orders, buys fresh product for a one-day sale, or shares a Digital Dozens link for emailed coupon redemption.
best_for: Schools, charities, teams, and community causes with access to a participating Krispy Kreme shop or supporters who can redeem Digital Dozens.
considerations: Local assortment, product cost, delivery, and pricing vary by participating shop.
The one-day format creates inventory risk; Digital Dozens redemption is restricted to participating dedicated U.S. shops.

programs.name: Pledge It Fundraising Suite
programs.summary: An integrated fundraising suite for donation forms, crowdfunding, peer-to-peer and pledge challenges, events, endurance, auctions, raffles, merchandise, sponsor packages, recurring giving, and participant fundraising.

content.summary: Pledge It is a subscription fundraising suite with peer-to-peer, per-unit pledges, events, endurance, sponsorships, auctions, raffles, and donation tools.

best_for: U.S. nonprofits and other eligible beneficiaries running activity challenges, endurance events, peer-to-peer campaigns, or events with sponsor packages.
considerations: A paid subscription and Stripe processing fees apply.
Flat gifts, performance pledges, and sponsorship sales have different processing and settlement flows.

programs.name: TeamFunder
programs.summary: A no-upfront revenue-share crowdfunding product for teams, high schools, and foundations using participant-led email, text, social, online, check, and phone donation outreach.

caveats: All TeamFunder fundraising and credit-card processing costs are included in the revenue-share agreement

participation_requirements: The school, team, activity, club, or foundation works with eTeamSponsor to create its campaign and participant outreach.
requirements.editorial_summary: TeamFunder is positioned for teams, schools, activities, clubs, and education foundations without an upfront license fee.

conditions: TeamFunder funds are due for remittance
caveats: Delivery may be ACH direct deposit or mailed check

notes: There is no campaign-length limit; eTeamSponsor recommends at least 90 days.
Participants send personalized email, text, and social appeals. Donations can be made online, by check, or by phone; the organization owns the campaign data and can use role-based reporting access.

programs.name: FundRaker
programs.summary: A licensed institutional crowdfunding product for higher education and advancement teams to centralize campus fundraising, events, giving days, advertising, sponsorships, ticketing, dashboards, and reporting.

value.description: Upfront annual license fee with renewal fee

caveats: Published pages do not provide a universal amount

arrangements.basis: Funds raised through the institution's licensed product

participation_requirements: The institution enters an annual license agreement and configures its payment gateway and campus fundraising users.
requirements.editorial_summary: FundRaker is the subscription product for higher education and institutional advancement.

notes: FundRaker uses payment-gateway integration for daily batches of deposits. Daily cadence is preserved in notes because the frozen payout-schedule enum supports only monthly and quarterly schedules.
Institutional users centralize campaign creation, giving days, events, sponsorships, ticketing, roles, dashboards, and reporting while deposits flow through the integrated gateway.

geography.notes: eTeamSponsor reports raising funds for schools nationwide. Campaigns can reach supporters anywhere in the world, but broader organization eligibility was not established.

content.summary: eTeamSponsor provides revenue-share team crowdfunding and licensed institutional fundraising for K–12 and higher education.
content.how_it_works: A school, team, or institution chooses TeamFunder's revenue-share campaign or FundRaker's annual license, configures participant and institutional outreach, and receives monthly or daily remittances according to product.
best_for: K–12 teams and activities seeking supported participant fundraising, or higher-education advancement teams centralizing crowdfunding, giving days, events, and sponsorships.
considerations: TeamFunder starts at an 80% organization share; FundRaker requires a quoted annual license.
The products have materially different remittance schedules and institutional scope.

programs.name: Box Tops for Education Program
programs.summary: Adult supporters buy participating products and scan paper receipts, submit digital receipts, or use connected retailer accounts so validated earnings are credited to an enrolled Pre-K–8 school.

caveats: Supporters purchase participating products in the ordinary course

value.description: Cash credit varies by participating product and any applicable bonus offer displayed in the app

arrangements.basis: Validated eligible purchase or bonus activity
conditions: Receipt or connected-account transaction is validated and credited to an active eligible school

arrangements.basis: Maximum cash earnings per enrolled school per program year
caveats: The program year runs March 2 through March 1

notes: The current official rules do not publish one universal per-product earning amount. December payments below $20 carry into the April payment.

participation_requirements: A school administrator enrolls the school, and the school must remain active and eligible.
Individual app users must be legal U.S. residents, at least 18, and register one account per email address and device.
Paper receipts must be scanned within 14 days of purchase unless earnings come through an eligible connected account or another permitted digital path.
other_restrictions: Private and parochial schools must qualify as 501(c)(3) educational organizations.
Eligible home-school associations must be IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) organizations with at least 15 students in Pre-K through grade 8.
Receipt reproduction, alteration, purchase, sale, trade, and other fraudulent submissions are prohibited.
requirements.editorial_summary: Eligible beneficiaries are public, qualifying private or parochial, military-operated, Puerto Rico accredited private or parochial, and qualifying home-school associations serving Pre-K through grade 8 under the published rules.

notes: School enrollment may take up to 30 days. Schools receive checks twice per school year, by December 31 and April 30. Semiannual anchored payments cannot be expressed by the frozen monthly/quarterly payout-schedule enum.

Supporters use the Box Tops app to scan a full receipt within 14 days, email eligible digital receipts, or link participating retailer accounts. Validated earnings post to the selected school's account, and General Mills mails checks to the school or an approved school PTO payee.

geography.notes: Eligible schools include the United States and most U.S. territories, accredited private or parochial schools in Puerto Rico, and qualifying U.S. military-operated schools worldwide. Individual app users must be adult U.S. legal residents.

content.summary: Box Tops for Education turns validated purchases of participating products into cash for enrolled Pre-K–8 schools.
content.how_it_works: Adult supporters select an eligible school in the app, buy participating products, and submit receipts or connect eligible retailer accounts; validated earnings accumulate for twice-yearly school checks.
best_for: Eligible Pre-K–8 schools and their PTOs seeking a passive purchase-linked program supported by family shopping.
considerations: School and supporter eligibility is tightly defined, and receipt submissions generally have a 14-day window.
Earning amounts vary by product and promotion, annual school earnings are capped at $20,000, and payments are made on two anchored school-year dates.
